## Final report

**Lightest all-PASS design: 1 mm copper**, areal mass 8.96 kg/m² — found at the second transport batch (evaluation 4 overall). It passed all four requirements: R1-screen 400 K (margin 19.9 K), R2-hotspot 332 K (margin 8 K), R3-mass 8.96 kg/m² (margin 91), R4-thickness 1 mm (margin 3.9 cm). This beats the prior campaign's best all-PASS design (10 mm graphite, 18 kg/m²) by roughly 50%.

**Why I stopped:** the constellation showed R2 (FE hotspot) is nearly flat with thickness for materials tested at 10–30 mm, but my thin-plate tests revealed that below ~10 mm, 2D spreading resistance dominates and hotspot rises sharply as thickness drops — governed almost entirely by conductivity. At the minimum allowed thickness (1 mm), I tested every material with conductivity between graphite and copper (graphite 150, aluminium_nitride 170, aluminium 200, copper 400): only copper's 400 W/m·K keeps the hotspot under the 340 K limit (332 K); aluminium misses by 0.19 K, aluminium nitride by 2.5 K, graphite by 4.4 K. Since layers must be whole millimetres, 1 mm is the minimum quantum, and copper is the only material that clears R2 at that thickness. Any multi-layer combination only adds mass on top of that minimum, so 8.96 kg/m² is a hard floor within this design space (materials × whole-mm layers).

**What I'd try next with more budget:** confirm titanium/stainless-steel at 1 mm fail even more decisively (low priority — dominated by conductivity), and probe whether a very thin copper cap (1 mm, heated face) plus a minimal-mass non-structural backing could ever be justified — though structurally it wouldn't reduce mass below the standalone 1 mm copper result, so I don't expect it to change the answer.
